issues.title: HTTPS links with and without :443 should not be duplicated
issues.body: An old report: exporting https://example.com:443/docs and https://example.com/docs creates two entries. Investigate whether this is already addressed on main before implementing another fix.

issues.title: Signed URLs lose meaning if query parameters are discarded
issues.body: The query string can contain signatures, repeated keys, tracking-looking keys or routing state. Add explicit regression coverage proving names, values, order and repetitions are preserved by normalization and all exports.

issues.title: Expose CSV output from the command line
issues.body: Add --format csv to the CLI using the library exporter. Related library work is required; default JSON behavior must remain compatible.

issues.title: Add CSV export for spreadsheet users
issues.body: Add a CSV exporter with a url header, stable first-seen deduplication, shared URL normalization and correct quoting. Keep this library change separate from CLI wiring.

issues.title: Collapse saved links that only differ after the hash
issues.body: Saving https://example.com/guide#a and https://example.com/guide#b produces two entries. Need an optional way to save one document entry rather than each section. Existing defaults must stay compatible.

issues.title: Bookmarks with different section anchors appear twice
issues.body: JSON export currently treats https://example.com/guide#intro and https://example.com/guide#install as different bookmarks. Add opt-in fragment-free identity while keeping current behavior the default. Shared normalizer, export and CLI should agree.

result.content:
import unittest

from bookmarks.urls import normalize_url


class URLTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_url_identity(self):
        self.assertEqual(normalize_url("HTTPS://Example.COM/articles?x=1#intro"),
                         "https://example.com/articles?x=1#intro")
        self.assertEqual(normalize_url("https://example.com"), "https://example.com/")

    def test_default_ports_share_identity(self):
        for first, second in (("https://example.com:443/a", "https://example.com/a"),
                              ("http://example.com:80/a", "http://example.com/a"),
                              ("https://[::1]:443/a", "https://[::1]/a")):
            self.assertEqual(normalize_url(first), normalize_url(second))
        self.assertEqual(normalize_url("https://example.com:8443/a"), "https://example.com:8443/a")

    def test_invalid_urls(self):
        for value in ("file:///etc/passwd", "javascript:alert(1)", "https:///path",
                      "https://user:pass@example.com", "https://example.com:bad",
                      "https://example.com:70000", "https://exa mple.com", "https://example.com/\n"):
            with self.subTest(value=value), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                normalize_url(value)


class ExportTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_export_reuses_url_identity(self):
        import json
        from bookmarks.exports import export_json
        result = json.loads(export_json(["HTTPS://Example.com", "https://example.com/"]))
        self.assertEqual(result, ["https://example.com/"])


class CLITests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_cli_exports_json(self):
        import json
        import subprocess
        import sys
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "bookmarks", "HTTPS://Example.com"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(result.stdout), ["https://example.com/"])

    def test_cli_rejects_bad_input(self):
        import subprocess
        import sys
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "bookmarks", "file:///etc/passwd"],
                                capture_output=True, text=True)
        self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertNotIn("Traceback", result.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

findings.title: Non-ASCII CSV URLs can crash the CLI
findings.description: `export_csv` retains non-ASCII URL characters, and the new `print(output)` call encodes them using the configured stdout encoding without handling encoding errors. With an ASCII-configured stdout, a URL such as `https://example.com/café` raises `UnicodeEncodeError`; the default JSON path escapes that character instead.

findings.title: Windows users get extra blank CSV rows
findings.description: `print(output)` sends the CSV exporter's `\r\n` line endings through stdout's Windows newline translation, producing `\r\r\n`. Every CSV row is affected when the CLI runs on Windows, so consumers can interpret the extra carriage returns as blank rows.
